region.text: the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg except Luxembourg City: today's Luxembourg and the Belgian province of Luxembourg

ledger.note: 1830: the Luxembourg countryside joins the revolt. 'most Luxembourgers joined the Belgian rebels' and took control of 'most of the Grand Duchy'; 'Only Luxembourg City, the capital and main fortress, stayed out of Belgian hands'. Month not given.

region.text: the province of Limburg except Maastricht, on both sides of today's border

ledger.note: 1830: Limburg, except Maastricht, goes with the revolution. The province 'was at first almost entirely under Belgian rule' after the 1830 revolution; the division 'began first with the separation of Maastricht' (my reading: Maastricht stayed Dutch). Month not given.

region.text: the Southern Provinces of the Netherlands in revolt, Brussels the seat of the Provisional Government

ledger.note: 1830: the Provisional Government in Brussels declares Belgian independence. 'The Provisional Government then issued a Declaration of Independence on 4 October 1830'; the Belgium page infobox gives independence from the Netherlands on 4 October 1830. The page names the Southern Provinces, not a boundary: the region is Cliopatria's 1840 outline.

region.text: the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg and the province of Limburg, the lands whose status the powers left open and the Dutch invasion contested

ledger.note: 1831: the Dutch army invades to reconquer Belgium. 'On 2 August 1831 the Dutch army, headed by the Dutch princes, invaded Belgium' (the Ten Days' Campaign); it failed after French military intervention. The Partitions of Luxembourg page adds that the Netherlands invaded 'to force it to accept a smaller territory', so the contested zone is the land the Netherlands wanted back, Luxembourg and Limburg (my reading; the page names no battlefield). The citadel of Antwerp was taken by Gerard on 23 December 1832.

region.text: the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg and the province of Limburg, divided by the treaty

ledger.note: 1839: the Treaty of London ends the dispute. 'Signed: 19 April 1839 in London' by the powers, the Netherlands and Belgium; Article VII made Belgium perpetually neutral. Fighting itself had ended with the French recapture of Antwerp in 1832 and an armistice; the land stayed in dispute until the treaty.

region.text: the remaining third of the Grand Duchy, today's Luxembourg

ledger.note: 1839: the eastern third of the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg goes back to William I. 'Belgium received about two-thirds of the grand duchy's territory, which became its new Province of Luxembourg. The remaining one-third, with about half the population, stayed in personal union with the Netherlands.' (Partitions of Luxembourg: 4,730 km2 to Belgium, including Arlon.) Cliopatria drops the cells at 1840.

region.text: eastern Limburg, today's Dutch province of Limburg except Maastricht

ledger.note: 1839: the eastern part of Limburg stays with the Netherlands. The province 'was divided in 1839 by the Treaty of London'; the western portion became a Belgian province, the eastern 'remained part of the Netherlands as the modern Dutch Province of Limburg'. Maastricht, never Belgian, is left out.

region.text: the Belgian Concession at Tientsin

ledger.note: 1902: Belgium obtains a concession at Tianjin. 'The Belgian Concession was established in 1902' (the envoy Maurice Joostens claimed the parcel after the Boxer rebels' defeat). The page gives no area; the radius is mine.

region.text: the Belgian Congo, formerly the Congo Free State

ledger.note: 1908: the Belgian state takes over the Congo. 'In 1908, this outcry led the Belgian state to assume responsibility for the government of the colony', 'henceforth called the Belgian Congo'. Before that the Free State was Leopold II's 'private possession' (1885).

region.text: Belgium, 2,598 of 2,636 communes by November 1914

ledger.note: 1914: Germany invades and occupies Belgium. 'On 4 August 1914, the German army invaded Belgium'; 'By November 1914, the vast majority of Belgian territory (2,598 out of 2,636 communes) was under German occupation'; the government went into exile at Le Havre while King Albert I commanded the army from Veurne. The unoccupied communes (about 1.4 per cent) are below the grid.

region.text: the Belgian zone of occupation in the Rhineland around Aachen and Krefeld, as Cliopatria draws it

ledger.note: 1918: the Belgian army occupies a zone of the Rhineland. 'Belgium maintained an army of occupation (Armée d'occupation, AO) in the Rhineland from 1918 to 1929', headquarters 'at Aachen', troops stationed in Krefeld. The page gives no month; the region is Cliopatria's own Belgian outline east of the border (1919 shape), counterpart the German state (the Cliopatria Weimar row begins in 1920).

region.text: occupied Belgium

ledger.note: 1918: the German occupation ends. 'On 11 November 1918, the German army signed an armistice. The final German troops left the country on 23 November.'

region.text: the Prussian districts of Eupen and Malmedy

ledger.note: 1920: Eupen and Malmedy pass to Belgium. The region was 'allocated to Belgium by the Treaty of Versailles', with 'the previously neutral territory of Moresnet'; the plebiscite was 'held between January and June 1920' and 'In June 1925, Eupen-Malmedy was finally incorporated into the Belgian state as part of Liège Province' (some 730 km2). Cliopatria draws it from 1919; the year here is the plebiscite's.

region.text: the industrial Ruhr district east of the Rhine

ledger.note: 1923: French and Belgian troops occupy the Ruhr. 'On 11 January 1923, French and Belgian troops occupied the industrial Ruhr district east of the Rhine.' Radius around Essen and Duisburg is my reading of 'the Ruhr district'.

region.text: Ruanda-Urundi

ledger.note: 1924: the League of Nations mandates Ruanda-Urundi to Belgium. 'in 1924 the League of Nations mandated them to Belgium'; drawn like the Congo as a dependency. Rwanda and Burundi are my reading of 'them' (the page's sentence is about the two kingdoms).

region.text: the industrial Ruhr district east of the Rhine

ledger.note: 1925: the Ruhr occupation ends. The Rhineland page is silent on the end of the Ruhr occupation (it says only 'On 11 January 1923, French and Belgian troops occupied the industrial Ruhr district'); the year is a bridging judgment, to be checked against the Occupation of the Ruhr page. [Reviewer eu-20-l, 2026-10-31: the Occupation of the Rhineland page does date it: the Ruhr occupation 'lasted until 25 August 1925' (timeline); month 8 and confidence 3 set]

region.text: the Belgian zone of occupation in the Rhineland

ledger.note: 1929: Belgium ends its occupation of the Rhineland. 'Belgium maintained an army of occupation ... in the Rhineland from 1918 to 1929'; the page's last evacuation is the French, 'on 30 June 1930'. Cliopatria drops the Rhineland cells at 1930.

region.text: the Belgian Concession at Tientsin

ledger.note: 1931: the Tianjin concession returns to China. 'an agreement to return the concession to China was signed in August 1929 and approved by the Belgian parliament in 1931'; the handover year is my reading of the approval.

region.text: Belgium except Eupen-Malmedy, occupied by Germany

ledger.note: 1940: Germany invades and occupies Belgium. 'German forces again invaded the country in May 1940'.

region.text: Eupen and Malmedy

ledger.note: 1940: Germany annexes Eupen-Malmedy again. 'Eupen-Malmedy was re-integrated into Germany' on 18 May 1940.

region.text: occupied Belgium

ledger.note: 1944: the liberation of Belgium begins. 'From September 1944 to February 1945 the Allies liberated Belgium'; the occupation is ended at its first year, and the last areas were freed by February 1945.

region.text: Eupen and Malmedy

ledger.note: 1945: Eupen-Malmedy is returned to Belgium. After a first liberation in autumn 1944, 'It was returned to Belgium in 1945.'

region.text: the Congo

ledger.note: 1960: the Congo becomes independent. 'The Belgian Congo gained independence in 1960 during the Congo Crisis'.

region.text: Ruanda-Urundi

ledger.note: 1962: Ruanda-Urundi becomes independent. 'Ruanda-Urundi followed with its independence two years later' (than the Congo, 1960).

wars.name: Belgian Revolution

zones.text: Luxembourg and Limburg, the lands left open between 1831 and 1839

wars.outcome: The Southern Provinces broke away in 1830; the Treaty of London of 19 April 1839 recognised Belgium as independent and perpetually neutral and divided Luxembourg and Limburg.
wars.note: Fighting 1830-1832 (the Dutch invasion of August 1831, the citadel of Antwerp taken 23 December 1832); the territorial dispute ran to 1839.

wars.name: Ten Days' Campaign
wars.outcome: The Dutch army invaded on 2 August 1831 and was stopped by French military intervention; no border changed.

wars.name: German occupation of Belgium during World War I

zones.text: Belgium, 2,598 of 2,636 communes occupied by November 1914

wars.outcome: Germany occupied nearly all of Belgium from August 1914; the armistice of 11 November 1918 and the last German troops' departure on 23 November restored the kingdom.

wars.name: Occupation of the Rhineland

zones.text: the Belgian zone around Aachen and Krefeld

wars.outcome: Belgium kept an army of occupation in the Rhineland from 1918 to 1929; the last evacuation (French) was on 30 June 1930.

wars.name: Occupation of the Ruhr
wars.outcome: French and Belgian troops occupied the Ruhr from 11 January 1923; the end date is not on the page opened.
wars.note: End year 1925 is a bridging judgment (confidence 1 in the ledger).

wars.name: World War II

zones.text: Belgium, invaded in May 1940 and liberated from September 1944 to February 1945

wars.outcome: German occupation of Belgium from May 1940 (Eupen-Malmedy annexed to Germany on 18 May 1940); liberated by the Allies between September 1944 and February 1945.

certainty.note: The Luxembourg and Limburg lines were a de facto front between rebels and the Netherlands, left open by the powers until the treaty.

Treaty borders from the Treaty of London (19 April 1839); the Tianjin concession (1902-1931) and the Rhineland zone (1918-1929) are occupation or concession lines set by agreement; Eupen-Malmedy a treaty line from 1920.

notes:
Written for batch eu-20-l (9 pages; budget up to 9). The Cliopatria row runs 1830..2024; the batch's period ends 1914, so 1915-2024 is reviewed from the same nine pages and thinly.

CLIOPATRIA ROWS TO CORRECT (all in keyframe_review): (1) the 1830-1833 shape holds none of the province of Luxembourg and keeps it in the Netherlands row; the pages say the rebels held most of Luxembourg and almost all of Limburg from 1830 (corrected to the 1834 shape); (2) the 1834-1839 shape includes Luxembourg City and Maastricht, which stayed out; (3) the 1885-1899 shape carries 52 cells of the lower Congo that belong to the Free State, not the Kingdom; (4) the Tianjin cells run 1900-1935 instead of 1902-1931; (5) the 1919-1929 shapes include the Belgian Rhineland zone and a Dutch strip joining it, which are occupation, not territory; (6) no shape for 1940-1944 (new keyframe) and the 1914-1918 shape ignores the occupation (ledger). The 1873, 1945 and 1950 one-cell changes are unexplained by any page: unverified: page budget.

PAGES THAT ARE SILENT: the Belgian Revolution and Treaty of London pages do not say what Belgium held in 1830-1839 (the Partitions of Luxembourg and Limburg (Belgium) pages do, in general terms); the Rhineland page gives no month for the Belgian arrival, does not say what the Belgians held after the British withdrawal of January 1926 (the 1926 shape change is not explained), and does not date the end of the Ruhr occupation (entered at confidence 1, 1925, to be checked on the Occupation of the Ruhr page). The page 'Belgian concession in Tianjin' did not load (url_not_found); the parent page was used.

GAZETTEER NAMES NEEDED: Eupen, Malmedy (places, Belgian Liège province), Ruhr (region); used in kingdom-of-belgium.

COUNTERPARTS THAT NEED DOSSIERS: ruanda-urundi (Belgian mandate 1924, trust territory to 1962; not in Cliopatria's Belgian rows as a separate state), luxembourg (the Grand Duchy before 1890, which Cliopatria's Luxembourg row does not cover; shares Q2719360 with duchy-of-luxembourg), german-empire / weimar-republic / nazi-germany (exist or belong to eu-20 and eu-21).

RULERS: none entered. The pages opened give only Leopold I (oath 21 July 1831), Leopold III's abdication in 1951 and Philippe's accession on 21 July 2013; a gap-filler should open 'List of Belgian monarchs'.

CAPITAL: the government sat at Le Havre in the First World War (page, no dates), King Albert I at Veurne; no capital_move was entered.
